solar-technician.intro: Learn to design, install, and maintain off-grid and mini-grid solar systems. From electrical fundamentals to commissioning a working installation.

skillDomains.name: Electrical Fundamentals
skillDomains.description: The non-negotiable foundation. Voltage, current, resistance, and the maths behind every system.

skills.name: DC Basics
skills.description: Understand direct current — what it is, how it flows, and why solar systems use it.

modules.title: What is direct current?
modules.content:
Direct current (DC) flows in one direction, always. Solar panels produce DC. Batteries store DC.

The grid delivers alternating current (AC) — it reverses direction 50 times per second (50 Hz in most of West Africa).

Your job as a solar technician begins with DC and only converts to AC at the end.

modules.title: Volts, amps, ohms, watts
modules.content:
Voltage (V)

The pressure pushing electrons.

Current (A)

The flow rate of electrons.

Resistance (Ω)

What slows the flow.

Ohm's Law

V = I × R

Power

P = V × I

Every calculation in solar work traces back to these two formulas.

steps.q: A 12V panel produces 5A. What is the power output?
A 24V battery bank runs a 6A load. What resistance does the circuit show?
A device draws 250W from a 12V battery. How much current?

modules.title: AC vs DC in a solar system
modules.content:
Every solar system has both:

  • DC side: panels → charge controller → battery
  • AC side: inverter → household sockets → appliances

The inverter is the bridge. It takes DC from the battery and produces AC for the house.

modules.prompt: A customer wants to power 6 LED bulbs (5W each) running 5 hours per night from a 12V battery system. Calculate the total energy needed and describe how you'd size the battery.
modules.context: Battery sizing is the first calculation in every off-grid system.
modules.placeholder:
Total daily energy (Wh):
Battery capacity needed (Ah):
Reasoning:
rubric: Converts to Ah at 12V: 150 Wh ÷ 12V = 12.5 Ah
Adds depth of discharge allowance (50% for lead-acid)
Arrives at a battery size of at least 30 Ah

modules.prompt: Draw a single-line diagram of an off-grid solar system showing: panels, charge controller, battery, inverter, and one load circuit.
steps: Sketch the layout on paper

skills.name: DC Circuits
skills.description: Series, parallel, and combined wiring — how to connect panels and batteries safely.

modules.title: Series vs parallel
modules.content:
Series

Positive of one connects to negative of the next. Voltages add, current stays the same.

Two 12V panels in series = 24V, same current.

Parallel

All positives together, all negatives together. Currents add, voltage stays the same.

Two 12V panels in parallel = 12V, double the current.

The rule

You choose series or parallel based on the charge controller's input limits.

steps.q: Two 12V, 5A panels in series. Output?
steps.f: Series: voltages add, current stays the same.

steps.q: Three 12V, 5A panels in parallel. Output?
steps.f: Parallel: currents add, voltage stays the same.

steps.q: Four 12V, 4A panels: two in series, then those pairs in parallel. Output?
steps.f: Two in series = 24V, 4A. Two such pairs in parallel = 24V, 8A.

modules.title: Choose a wiring configuration
modules.prompt: A client has 4 panels (250W, 30V, 8.5A each) and a 24V MPPT charge controller rated for 100V input maximum and 40A output. Describe how you would wire the panels and why.
modules.context: Wiring configuration is constrained by the controller's voltage and current limits.
rubric: Considers series vs parallel for voltage
Notes that 4 in series = 120V exceeds the 100V controller limit
Checks that current stays within the 40A output range

skillDomains.name: Electrical Safety
skillDomains.description: Protect yourself and your clients. Solar work involves DC arcs, batteries, and roof work.

skills.name: DC Hazards
skills.description: Why DC is more dangerous than most people think.

modules.title: DC arcs don't let go
modules.content:
Most people fear AC. Solar technicians learn to fear DC more.

AC current crosses zero 100 times per second, which means an AC arc self-extinguishes. DC current is constant — a DC arc will sustain itself and can reach thousands of degrees.

What this means in practice

  • Never disconnect DC under load without a proper DC-rated switch
  • Never work on live DC circuits if you can isolate
  • A DC short across a battery bank can melt tools in under a second
  • Battery terminals must always be covered when not being worked on

modules.title: Battery safety
modules.content:
Lead-acid batteries

  • Release explosive hydrogen during charging — ventilate
  • Contain sulphuric acid — eye protection always
  • Produce high short-circuit currents — insulated tools only

Lithium batteries

  • Can enter thermal runaway if overcharged or damaged
  • Require a Battery Management System (BMS)
  • Never charge below 0°C

Universal rules

  • Remove metal jewellery before working
  • Use insulated tools only
  • Have a Class C fire extinguisher nearby

steps.q: You're about to work on a lead-acid battery bank. First thing?
o: Put on eye protection and remove metal jewellery
steps.f: PPE first. Always.

steps.q: You need to disconnect a battery terminal. Which order?
steps.f: Negative first when disconnecting.

steps.q: You smell rotten eggs near the battery bank. What does this mean?
o: Hydrogen sulphide — ventilation failure, evacuate immediately
steps.f: Rotten egg smell is hydrogen sulphide from overcharging.

modules.title: Battery acid splash response
modules.prompt: While servicing a lead-acid battery bank, acid splashes onto your forearm and a small amount reaches your eye. Walk through exactly what you do, in order.
modules.context: Fast, correct action prevents permanent injury.
rubric: Flush the eye with clean running water for at least 20 minutes
Flush the skin simultaneously or immediately after
Do NOT neutralise with baking soda on skin

skillDomains.name: System Design & Sizing
skillDomains.description: Design systems that meet real client needs without over- or under-sizing.

skills.name: Load Audit
skills.description: Determine how much energy a client actually needs.

modules.title: Start with the load, always
modules.content:
You cannot size a system until you know what it must power. This is the load audit.

For every appliance the client wants to run, record:

  • Power draw in watts (from the label)
  • Hours per day it runs
  • Whether it runs during daylight or at night

Multiply watts × hours to get watt-hours (Wh) per day.

steps.q: 4 LED bulbs (10W each) running 6 hours per night. Energy per day?
Add a TV (60W) running 4 hours per night. New total?
Add a phone charging (5W) 3 hours per day and a fan (25W) 8 hours per night. Total?

modules.title: Run a real load audit
modules.prompt: A small shop wants solar power for: 8 LED bulbs (7W each) for 6 hours, a fridge (150W) running 24 hours, a phone charging station (30W) for 4 hours, and a radio (15W) for 5 hours. Calculate the daily energy requirement.
modules.context: This is a typical small-business solar job.

modules.title: Design a load audit form
modules.prompt: Create a one-page form you can use during client visits to collect load information.
steps: Include columns for appliance, watts, hours, and total Wh
Add a section for peak-load identification
Add a section for future loads
Design it to be filled in a 20-minute visit
Test it on a real or simulated client

skills.name: Battery Sizing
skills.description: Choose the right battery capacity for autonomy and cycle life.

modules.title: How much storage do you need?
modules.content:
Battery capacity is measured in amp-hours (Ah) or kilowatt-hours (kWh).

The formula

Battery Ah = (Daily Wh × Days of autonomy) ÷ (System voltage × Depth of discharge)

Rules of thumb

  • Days of autonomy: 1–2 days for reliable grid backup, 2–3 days for off-grid
  • Depth of discharge (DoD): 50% for lead-acid, 80% for lithium
  • System losses: add 20%

steps.q: Daily energy is 2000 Wh. System is 24V. 2 days of autonomy. Lead-acid (50% DoD). Required Ah?
Same system but lithium (80% DoD). Required Ah?
Why do lithium batteries need less Ah than lead-acid for the same job?
steps.f: 80% DoD vs 50% DoD means you use more of the capacity you paid for.

modules.title: Choose a battery type
modules.prompt: A client has a budget of 500,000 Le for batteries, needs 5 kWh storage, and wants the system to last at least 5 years. Should they go lead-acid or lithium? Explain your reasoning.
modules.context: Battery choice is the single biggest cost and lifetime decision in an off-grid system.
rubric: Accounts for cycle life (lead-acid ~1500 cycles, lithium ~4000+)
Calculates cost per usable kWh over 5 years
Makes a clear recommendation with reasoning

skillDomains.name: Installation
skillDomains.description: Mount, wire, and connect. The hands-on work that brings the design to life.

skills.name: Panel Mounting
skills.description: Install panels on roofs and ground mounts safely and at the correct angle.

modules.title: Where and how to mount panels
modules.content:
Roof mounting

  • South-facing in West Africa (north of the equator)
  • Tilt angle roughly equals the latitude
  • Must withstand wind loads
  • Never penetrate roofing without proper sealing

Ground mounting

  • Easier maintenance access
  • Better airflow = cooler panels = more output
  • Must be theft-resistant

Shading

A single shaded cell can reduce output of an entire panel by 50%+. Avoid shade at all costs.

modules.title: Best practices for mounting
modules.content:
Before you drill

  • Confirm roof structure can bear the weight
  • Check for existing wiring under the roof
  • Plan the layout so cable runs are short and equal

During mounting

  • Leave 5-10cm gap between panels for airflow
  • Use stainless steel bolts — zinc ones rust quickly
  • Tighten to the manufacturer's torque spec

After mounting

  • Confirm all bolts are tight
  • Confirm grounding is correct
  • Confirm no roof leaks

steps.q: Your site is at 12°N latitude. What tilt angle for the panels?
steps.f: In West Africa, tilt angle roughly equals latitude.

steps.q: A tree partially shades panels for 2 hours each morning. What do you do?
o: Move the panels or cut the tree
steps.f: 2 hours of shade can reduce daily output by 15–30%. Fix the shade.

steps.q: Why use stainless steel bolts instead of zinc?
o: Zinc rusts in tropical climate within 1–2 years
steps.f: Tropical humidity accelerates corrosion.

modules.title: Design a mounting layout
modules.prompt: For a 6-panel system (250W each), design the roof layout. Draw a top-down view showing panel positions, tilt, spacing, and cable runs.
steps: Choose the optimal direction based on hemisphere
Set the tilt angle for your latitude
Draw the panel positions with airflow gaps
Route cables to minimise length
Mark all mounting points

skills.name: Wiring & Connections
skills.description: Wire the DC side safely and to code.

modules.title: Sizing DC cables
modules.content:
Cable size determines two things:

  • Voltage drop (larger cables = less loss)
  • Current-carrying capacity (larger cables = higher safe current)

The rule

  • Aim for <3% voltage drop on DC circuits
  • Use the manufacturer's ampacity table
  • When in doubt, go one size larger

Common sizes in solar

  • Panel wiring: 4mm² typical
  • Battery to inverter: 25–50mm² depending on current
  • Controller to battery: 6–16mm²

modules.title: Choose a battery cable
modules.prompt: A 24V system has a 3000W inverter 2 metres from the battery. Calculate the current draw, then choose a suitable cable size.
modules.context: Battery cables carry the highest currents in a solar system.
rubric: Notes that peak current may be higher (surge loads)
Considers 2m round-trip = 4m of cable for voltage drop
Specifies proper fuse or breaker rating

skillDomains.name: Commissioning & Maintenance
skillDomains.description: Test the system, hand it over to the client, and keep it running.

skills.name: System Testing
skills.description: Verify everything works before you leave.

modules.title: Never hand over an untested system
modules.content:
Commissioning is the formal handover of a working system.

Test in this order

  1. Open-circuit voltage of the panel array
  2. Short-circuit current of the panel array (using a clamp meter)
  3. Charge controller is in correct mode
  4. Battery voltage at rest and under load
  5. Inverter output — voltage and frequency on the AC side
  6. Load test — turn on all loads and confirm the system holds

Document every reading.

steps.q: A 250W panel reads 37V open circuit. Manufacturer spec says 37.6V. Acceptable?
steps.f: Within ±5% is normal.

steps.q: Panel array reads 20V open circuit but spec says 74V. What's wrong?
o: Likely incorrect wiring (parallel instead of series)
steps.f: 20V is roughly one panel's voltage. Check the wiring.

steps.q: Inverter output reads 195V AC. Client expects 230V. What do you check?
steps.f: Low AC output usually traces to low DC input.

modules.title: Write a commissioning report
modules.prompt: Design a commissioning report template you'd fill in for every installation and give to the client at handover.
steps: List every test and its expected value
Include a place for measured values
Add a sign-off section for client acceptance
Include a warranty and contact section
Add basic operating instructions

skills.name: Maintenance
skills.description: Keep systems running for their full lifetime.

modules.title: Preventive vs reactive
modules.content:
Preventive maintenance

  • Clean panels monthly
  • Check battery water levels monthly (lead-acid)
  • Inspect all cable connections quarterly
  • Test system output under load quarterly

Reactive maintenance

  • Responding to client calls about failures
  • Diagnosing and repairing

A well-maintained system lasts 15–25 years. A neglected one fails in 3–5.

steps.q: How often should solar panels be cleaned in dusty West African conditions?
steps.f: Monthly is the baseline. During harmattan, every 2 weeks.

steps.q: A client's system output has dropped 15% over 6 months. Most likely cause?
steps.f: Gradual output loss almost always means dust.

steps.q: Which maintenance task is most often neglected and most expensive to fix later?
steps.f: Lead-acid batteries that run dry are destroyed.
